sources.holds: ms.tex (sha256 4c417baf0b7b847ad102f8d6ec11da3adfe13cf20e754565a412f5488333b33f): the table 'Candidates Accepted By Our Pipeline' (period and planet radius, each with a lower and an upper error); the table 'Number of Planets Per Star Versus Orbital Period (In Percentage)' (seven radius bins from 0.5 to 4.0 Earth radii by five period bins from 0.5 to 200 days, each cell with its errors or a one-sigma upper limit and, in parentheses, the fraction of injected planets recovered in the cell; two sets of entries for two choices of stellar radii); the text of the calculation (2543 stars; the mean geometric transit probability over the sample's stars times 1.08; each candidate weighted by one minus a radius-dependent false-positive probability taken from Table 1 of the false-positive paper; a median stellar radius of 0.47 solar radii and no stellar mass stated); the table 'Injected Planets' as ten rows, published in its entirety only in the journal's electronic edition

X1.occurrenceAuthentic.why: An exposure is the recovered fraction times the number of stars times the transit probability of the sample's stars. The fetched files hold the first two for every cell; the third needs the stars' radii and masses, which the paper takes from a stellar catalogue it does not print, and the archive that serves that catalogue was under maintenance. A transit probability made up from one median radius and a guessed mass would be a number of this session's, so no contract was written and nothing was computed from the files.
requests: From the NASA Exoplanet Archive (TAP, table q1_q16_stellar): kepid, teff, logg, radius, mass for teff < 4000 and logg > 3, the parent sample the paper names (it gives 4915 stars), with the archive's terms page and the retrieval date
From the journal's page of the article of R1-a, with its terms: the table 'Injected Planets' in its entirety and, if it is published there, the list of the 2543 selected stars

Then, before any estimate: an amendment fixing the contract (the first set of entries of the occurrence table as the target; one problem per period bin over the seven radius bins; the candidates of the candidates table with the larger of the two radius errors; the reliability from Table 1 of R1-b; the exposure from the recovered fraction, 2543 stars and the mean transit probability times 1.08 over the fetched stars; the bound: each compared cell inside the published errors), and the kernel's own resolution record for these bins, which are 0.5 Earth radii wide

X2.massFunctionAuthentic.why: No file of R2 was fetched: the catalogue service (CDS, Strasbourg) did not connect on 2026-11-10; a mirror answered one availability probe, of which nothing was kept and nothing read.
requests: R2 of thresholds.json as written: a cluster's member list with each member's mass (or a luminosity and the relation that gives one) and its stated uncertainty, the survey's completeness as a function of magnitude, and the cluster's published present-day mass function as a table with the paper's text and the terms; the catalogue is for the person fetching to name from its own ReadMe
Then, before any estimate: an amendment fixing the contract (bins of the published function, the exposure from the stated completeness, the bound)

X3.citedImplementation.why: Running a downloaded implementation is not permitted (DECISIONS_2026-11-07.md, 264 rulings, item 4). Nothing of R4 was fetched: the text of R1-a's calculation names no implementation of a binned-rate likelihood (it divides a smoothed map of the candidates by a smoothed map of the search completeness), so there was no implementation to name from the documentation of R1's calculation, as R4 asks.
requests: R4 of thresholds.json as written, once a calculation is chosen whose documentation names such an implementation; and Carl's permission to run it
